summary: Exported MainActivity, SystemJobService, ShareChooserPendingIntent, FirebaseInstanceIdReceiver, DiagnosticsReceiver and ProfileInstallReceiver expose the app to external invocation. CLEAR_TEXT traffic enabled and a large set of dangerous permissions including INTERNET, BILLING, READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, WAKE_LOCK, Ad ID, and many launcher badge permissions increase attack surface.
attack_surface: Exported activities and services that can be started by other apps
Exported receivers with no protection allowing arbitrary broadcasts
Use of CLEAR_TEXT network traffic exposing credentials
GrantUriPermissions on several FileProviders permitting external read/write
Wide range of dangerous permissions enabling deep system access
top_risks: External apps can invoke MainActivity without authentication
Broadcast receivers can be triggered maliciously to execute code
Cleartext network traffic allows credential interception
FileProviders can be misused to exfiltrate data
High number of dangerous permissions may facilitate privilege escalation
abuse_hypotheses: An attacker could start MainActivity via an intent to cause unintended navigation or data exposure
Sending a broadcast to ShareChooserPendingIntent could trigger unintended content sharing
Intercepting FCM messages via FirebaseInstanceIdReceiver could flood device with malicious notifications
Exploit DiagnosticsReceiver or ProfileInstallReceiver to dump diagnostic data or install malicious profiles
Using grantUriPermissions to access files on external storage from outside the app
recommended_next_steps: Restrict or remove explicit exported components, adding protecting permissions where appropriate
Disable CLEAR_TEXT traffic or enforce HTTPS only via network_security_config
Revoke unneeded dangerous permissions and use permission request on runtime
Review and secure all third‑party library manifests, especially Firebase and Google Play Services
Consider disabling grantUriPermissions unless required for inter‑app file sharing
